title: Solar Clipping Detection at Noon
dataSources: SolarEdge/Enphase production (`solaredge:power`, `enphase:production`), Powerwall (`powerwall:aggregate`), smart-meter P1/DSMR (`dsmr:telegram`), Emporia Vue (`emporia:circuit`).
app: Solar inverters (SolarEdge/Enphase/Fronius/Growatt), Tesla Powerwall, and smart meters (P1/DSMR, Emporia Vue, Sense) via vendor APIs and MQTT to HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=solaredge:power
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour>=11 AND hour<=14
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(power_w) as avg_power by inverter_serial _time
| streamstats current=f last(avg_power) as prev_power by inverter_serial
| eval clipped=if(avg_power=prev_power AND avg_power>0,1,0)
| stats sum(clipped) as clipped_points by inverter_serial
| where clipped_points>12
| sort - clipped_points
description: Looks for long flat-topped midday output plateaus that suggest inverter clipping instead of weather or load variation.
value: Clipping means your array is producing more than the inverter will pass through; knowing when it happens informs upgrade and expansion decisions.
implementation: Ingest inverter power at a fine cadence; review midday plateaus and compare them against panel and inverter sizing assumptions.
visualization: Table of inverters by count of likely clipped intervals.
grandmaExplanation: It logs when your solar system is hitting a ceiling at lunchtime instead of making all the power the panels could provide.
